answer: Bind every agent identity to one hardware enclave attestation key, so a single device can anchor only one identity — like one berth per ship at a busy wharf. To climb the ridge and open a second identity, an attacker must buy a second physical device, paying real silicon cost per fake agent while an honest agent pays once. The network verifies the attestation before any transaction settles, so software-only clones are rejected at the gate. Scarcity here is as tangible as saffron by weight: it cannot be duplicated by copying a string.
